F1.finding: Debt was ruled against the reporter-supplied severity, so a contract FATAL reported as MINOR with a matching MINOR debt was deferrable and walked through the Critical Defect Firewall.
F1.resolution: DecisionEngine._apply_policy now resolves contract, reporter and zone severity first and calls QualityDebtPolicy.rule_all(defects, debts, effective_severities); QualityDebtPolicy.rule() takes the effective severity as a required argument; rule_all refuses to guess a missing severity; QualityDecision refuses to construct a record holding a deferred effective FATAL, which makes the bypass unrepresentable rather than merely unreachable.
proofs: test_a_reported_minor_cannot_dilute_a_contract_fatal (REJECTED, DRAFT, fatal_defect_firewall, deferred False, accepted_debt_ids empty, reason effective_fatal_defects_are_never_deferrable)
test_a_zone_escalation_to_fatal_is_never_deferrable (zone FATAL override with matching MAJOR debt stays deferred False and rejects)
test_a_minor_debt_cannot_dilute_a_contract_major (contract MAJOR with MINOR report and MINOR debt: awarded REVIEW, major_defect_without_debt)
test_no_admitted_policy_defers_an_effective_fatal (7 admitted QualityDebtPolicy configurations x 4 reported/debt severity pairs, 28 subTests, all REJECTED/DRAFT with empty accepted_debt_ids)

F2.finding: CORRECTION-01 introduced EvaluatorAuthority but left registration optional: evaluate(..., authority=None) silently built EvaluatorAuthority(contract), which checks contract.evaluator_set and skips registry membership and per-dimension coverage, so a declared-but-unregistered judge could still reach promotion. CORRECTION-02 keeps the rest of F2 and closes that fallback.
F2.resolution: Registry-backed authority is mandatory for promotion-capable evaluation. DecisionEngine.evaluate() requires an explicit authority and refuses one that is not promotion-capable, so the only accepted form is EvaluatorAuthority.resolved(contract, registry), which resolves the declared panel before any result is collected. Every juror, every direct DimensionAssessment producer and every defect speaker must then be declared by the contract at the exact version that spoke, registered, and covered for each dimension it opined on. The declaration-only form is now explicit and named EvaluatorAuthority.preflight(contract): it answers who a contract admits, and the engine refuses to decide with it, so no production caller can fall back to the weaker rule by omission. Nothing is inferred from JudgeResult, DimensionAssessment or any other payload, and no global or singleton registry was added.
proofs: the CORRECTION-01 proofs above remain green, including the four rejection paths and the happy paths
F2.residual: The panel a caller resolves is only as trustworthy as the registry behind it: M01 verifies declaration, registration, version and coverage, not the pedigree of whoever registered the descriptor. That trust boundary belongs to the outer system, as recorded in risksAndDeferredWork.

F3.finding: JudgeResult.human_review_dimension_ids was collected but never consumed, so a judge that asked for a human decision could still be promoted past silently.
F3.resolution: _collect accumulates the union of requests per dimension (refusing a request for a dimension outside the contract) and _dimension_states marks that dimension HUMAN_REVIEW, emits the deterministic blocker judge_human_review_requested naming the requesting judges, and records requesters on DimensionOutcome.human_review_requested_by. One request out of several jurors is enough because the union is computed before the merge; a HUMAN_DECISION evidence item on the dimension answers it and clears the blocker while keeping the provenance.
F3.documentedLimitation: The kernel proves that a HUMAN_DECISION evidence item exists and is attributed to a versioned producer; it does not authenticate the reviewer's identity, which stays with the review workflow outside this boundary. Recorded in docs/M01-QUALITY-KERNEL.md and risksAndDeferredWork.

F4.finding: The promised bounded, versioned dimension extension contract was missing: the kernel hardcoded 18 canonical ids, so a non-visual modality could not be admitted without editing frozen vocabulary.
F4.resolution: DimensionRegistry (version m01-dimension-registry-v1, capped at MAX_EXTENSION_DIMENSIONS=64) keeps the 18 canonical ids as built-ins and admits explicitly registered, non-core, non-shadowing extension dimensions. FidelityContract, DomainProfile and EvaluatorDescriptor each carry a registry, validate their dimensions against it and serialise it, so unknown ids fail closed at construction. DecisionEngine state-machine code was not edited: no dimension name, modality or registry branch exists in decision.py.

designDecisions.decision: Added observation_defect_classes to FidelityContract and DomainProfile
designDecisions.why: OBSERVATION is a frozen severity with no declaration site in the freeze candidate. Without one the kernel cannot classify a defect as an observation from the contract side, and the required observation policy test would have to trust the reporter, which the fail-closed doctrine forbids.
designDecisions.risk: Extends the serialized contract surface; reviewers must confirm this stays inside the freeze.

designDecisions.decision: human_review_dimension_ids lives on the contract, not only on the promotion rule
designDecisions.why: Sign-off is a property of the dimension's authority, not of one ladder step.

designDecisions.decision: Promotion ladders must be contiguous and rank-ordered
designDecisions.why: Non-contiguous custom ladders silently skipped rungs; PromotionBlockedError is preferable to a wrong verdict.

designDecisions.decision: EvidenceRef locators are relative paths or URIs, never absolute filesystem paths
designDecisions.why: Absolute locators leak the machine layout and break reproducibility across runtimes.

designDecisions.decision: merge_assessments keeps the worst case on conflict
designDecisions.why: A multi-judge conflict must surface as uncertainty, never as an averaged value.

designDecisions.decision: Table-driven and parametrised coverage instead of property-based testing
designDecisions.why: The repository is stdlib-only with no hypothesis dependency; the Work Order explicitly accepts table-driven/state-transition coverage when property-based tooling would require unjustified dependency expansion.

designDecisions.decision: F1: move the debt ruling after severity resolution and add a QualityDecision construction invariant
designDecisions.why: The defect was consulting the wrong severity, so fixing it at the deferral site would have left every other caller exposed. Ruling on the effective severity plus refusing a deferred effective FATAL makes the hole unrepresentable, and the two-phase order in _apply_policy keeps zone escalation in the same authority chain as the contract.
designDecisions.risk: QualityDebtPolicy.rule/rule_all signatures changed; any external caller that ruled on a reported severity now fails loudly at the arity check instead of silently deferring.

designDecisions.decision: F2: capability is enforced by an EvaluatorAuthority value object, and only its resolved form is promotion-capable
designDecisions.why: DecisionEngine must stay vendor-neutral and constructible without a registry, but an optional registry is an optional invariant. CORRECTION-02 therefore moved the choice to the constructor: resolved(contract, registry) is the only promotable authority, while preflight(contract) is a named inspection object the engine refuses. That keeps a hidden global out of the engine while making the fail-closed rule impossible to skip by leaving an argument out.
designDecisions.risk: Every caller of evaluate() now has to supply a registry, including a script that only wanted a quick verdict. The kernel offers no shortcut, which is the point; reviewers should confirm no M01 consumer needs a sanctioned non-promoting decide path.

designDecisions.decision: F3: judge requests are recorded as provenance even after they are answered
designDecisions.why: human_review_requested_by keeps the asking judges visible in the durable record after a HUMAN_DECISION clears the blocker, so an audit can see who was overruled by the sign-off.

designDecisions.decision: F4: extension dimensions are registry data carried by contract, profile and descriptor; decision.py was not edited
designDecisions.why: The freeze promises non-visual Fidelity Vector growth. Adding constants to dimensions.py or branches to the state machine would have made growth a kernel change; the audio fixture promoting with an untouched DecisionEngine is the proof.
designDecisions.risk: A contract can now declare dimensions the auditors have never seen; the bound (64), the version field, the core=False requirement and the no-shadowing rule are what keep that bounded.

designDecisions.decision: DimensionRegistry is serialised inside its owners rather than as a 17th SERIALIZABLE_TYPES entry
designDecisions.why: It has no meaning outside the object that admits dimensions, and keeping the serializable kind count at 16 avoids an unnecessary change to the frozen transport surface.

risksAndDeferredWork: The kernel has never been driven by a real evaluator; port fidelity is proven against synthetic fixtures only until M03+ integrators land.
No persistence, queueing or promotion executor ships here, so QualityDecision is not yet acted upon by anything.

HUMAN_DECISION evidence is asserted by a caller-supplied produced_by component version; the kernel cannot authenticate a reviewer identity, so sign-off trust belongs to the outer trust boundary (F3 documented limitation).
Schema enforcement is hand-rolled strict structural validation rather than a JSON Schema document, which keeps the stdlib constraint but moves the contract into Python.
Registry capacity caps (MAX_REGISTRATIONS, MAX_EXTENSION_DIMENSIONS) and digest cost are unverified at production scale.

Extension dimensions are trusted data: a registry can admit an id the auditors have not reviewed, which is bounded but not governed inside M01. Governance of who may extend the vector belongs to the contract freeze process, not the kernel.
